predecessors.name: Songhai Empire
predecessors.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

successors.name: Sokoto Caliphate
successors.text: Kebbi: Leka, Surame and Birnin Kebbi in the Rima and Zamfara valleys (the page gives no outline)

ledger.x: 1516-7: Kanta Kuta revolts and Kebbi breaks from Songhai.
under Muhammad Kanta (took power probably 1523-24): Kebbi "had conquered vast territories and exacted tributes from much of Hausaland".
by the mid-17th century: the Kebbi empire declines.
1808: the Kingdom of Kebbi ends as a Hausa power; Muhammadu Hodi resists in the Zamfara valley and Karari at Argungu (survivors, later the Kebbi Emirate of Argungu).

wars.name: Songhai-Kebbi wars
wars.outcome: Songhai tried to restore control in 1517-18 and failed; Kanta routed the armies of Askia Muhammad Bunkan ("a crushing defeat") and no later Askia attacked Kebbi again.

wars.name: Kebbi-Bornu war
wars.outcome: "Bornu invaded Hausa states under Kanta's control, however he routed their armies."

wars.name: Fulani conquest of Kebbi
wars.outcome: Abdullahi dan Fodio defeated Kebbi in 1808 and founded Gwandu; Muhammadu Hodi and Karari resisted; after Karari died in 1831 his son Yakubu Nabame surrendered; Argungu was recognised as independent in 1867.

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the imperial reach under Kanta was tribute, not annexation.
